_comment: The drone's body for the physics twin (twin/), part by part.
Masses and watts are the parts list's (~/delta-video/calc.py: estimates
from 2026 listings). Places and sizes are a first layout, not CAD: they
decide where the centre of mass sits and what can hit what, so check them
against the real frame once it is built.
Frame: the frame's own. Origin at the centre of the ball, which is also
the gimbal's pivot. +x forward, +y left, +z up -- MuJoCo's (and ROS's)
size: box = full lengths [x, y, z]; cylinder = [radius, length].
at: one centre, or a list of centres sharing the part's mass equally.
watts: average electrical draw of the electronics, before the 5 V

parts.name: frame plate
parts._: the 5-inch carbon frame's 110 g: 50 g of centre plates, 60 g of arms (below)

parts.name: arms
parts._: four carbon arms, centre to each motor

parts.name: motors
parts._: upside down under the arm ends

parts.name: battery
_: 4S2P Li-ion, 8 x Molicel P42A (21 x 70 mm). Stood on end, 2 x 4: lying
flat (84 x 70 mm) its corners are inside the propeller discs, which sit
at the same height. Hanging low also makes the frame a pendulum in the
gimbal: it levels itself when the motors are off.

parts.name: lidar
parts._: LD06, on top: the props are underneath, so nothing cuts its ring but the cage

motors.name: EMAX ECO II 2207 2400KV, 5-inch 3-blade props
motors._wheelbase: motor to opposite motor, a typical 5-inch frame. PENDING: the real frame's
motors._spin: PX4's quad X: +1 turns counter-clockwise seen from above, and twists the frame the other way

_: EMAX publishes no table for the ECO II 2207 2400KV. These rows are the
ECO III 2207 2400KV (the same size and KV, the next version) on an
AVAN 5026 3-blade at 16.8 V, from a reseller's listing; max_grams is
the ECO II's listed maximum on 4S, max_watts the ECO III's. Hover
(~370 g a motor) falls inside the rows. REPLACE with our own thrust
stand test once the motors arrive.

motors._spin_up: seconds: time constant of the motor reaching a new speed. ASSUMED (typical 5-inch, ESC braking on)
motors._idle: of full speed, while armed: the ESC's idle so the motors never stall
motors._rotor_inertia: kg m^2: prop (4.5 g, ~r^2/3) + bell (~15 g at 13 mm). ESTIMATE; speeding a rotor up twists the frame
motors._shaft_efficiency: motor + ESC, electrical in to shaft out: for the props' twisting torque. ASSUMED

_: Three bearings in a row, so the cage can roll any way while the frame
keeps its own: frame -(left/right)- inner ring -(front/back)- outer
ring -(top/bottom)- cage. The parts list's 4 ring bearings + 2 cage
gimbal._friction: N m: each bearing pair's dry friction. ESTIMATE (small ball bearings)

cage._: a thin shell: inertia 2/3 m r^2. Only the cage touches anything

air._drag_area: m^2, drag coefficient x frontal area of cage + drone. ESTIMATE: the cage is mostly holes. Measure with a coast-down test

floor._rolling: m: MuJoCo's rolling friction = rolling resistance x cage radius (0.05 x 0.225, calc.py's hard floor)
